lpi.basis: Range spans FHWA PedSafe Phase II $2,600 per intersection capital cost including materials, installation and engineering labor and FHWA-cited $200 controller-only to $1,200 per signal retiming cost consistent with NYC DOT $1,200 average, with FHWA Proven Safety Countermeasures noting costs are very low when only signal timing alteration is required.
lpi.item: adding a leading pedestrian interval (signal timing change) at an existing signalized intersection

turn_ban.basis: Range spans FHWA low-cost program reporting $150 for lane-use signs for illegal turning movements and PBIC guidance of $30 to $150 per NO TURN ON RED sign plus $200 installation (~$230-$350/sign, ~$460-$1,400 for 2-4 signs per peak-hour restriction with enforcement by existing patrols).

citations.title: Low Cost Traffic Engineering Improvements - What Agencies Are Using Low Cost Improvements?

turn_ban.item: a peak-hour turn restriction at an intersection (signs and enforcement)

hardened_centerline.basis: Virginia DOT states left-turn hardening elements (modular curbs and vertical delineators) typically cost $2,000-$4,500 per intersection,, matching NYC DOT's hardened centerline of rubber curb and bollards/delineators.
hardened_centerline.item: a hardened centerline (rubber curbs and flexible delineator posts) at one intersection

daylighting.basis: Low end is Hoboken paint-and-plastic-post starting cost of ~$1,500 per intersection consistent with FHWA PEDSAFE delineators ~$50-$100 plus signs ~$200; high end is NYC Council/NYC DOT hardened-barrier estimate of $9,900 per intersection for barrier materials, rails and signage, corroborated by NYC DOT-cited Portland average of $8,000 per intersection.

daylighting.item: daylighting an intersection corner (removing parking near the crosswalk, with markings or flexible posts)

split_phase.basis: Range spans FHWA Low-Cost Traffic Engineering Improvements and Michigan case study FHWA-SA-09-015, covering retiming-only protected-phase addition to controller plus signal-head and retiming work per intersection.
split_phase.item: adding a protected turn phase / split phase to an existing signal (retiming, signal heads)

retime.basis: FHWA ATSPM reports ~$4,500 per intersection for 3-5 year retiming and USDOT ITS evaluation reports ~$3,000 per signal for timing updates, spanning $3,000-$4,500.

citations.title: The National Transportation Operators Coalition estimates that upgrading and retiming the US's traffic signals over 10 years would cost $1.125 billion annually

retime.item: retiming a traffic signal (cycle length and splits) at one intersection
